name: PDK4
summary: PDK4, pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4, on chromosome 4 - a gene of muscle metabolism whose product shifts a cell from burning glucose toward burning fat. At one variant (g.38973231A>G, in intron 2; BIEC2-903605), A/A and A/G horses were over-represented among elite Thoroughbred racehorses in a 2010 study; a Quarter Horse study did not find the same difference. The A allele was commoner in Quarter Horses and the G allele in Arabians in another study. A/A and A/G horses rated about 16 lb higher on the handicap scale than G/G in that sample. These are associations with race performance, not a proven causal speed allele: the authors said the causal variant was still to be found. A is the reference allele and probably the ancestral one: horses from before domestication carried it. G is derived but old, not a product of racing.

phenotypes.name: PDK4 A/A
phenotypes.description: Two A copies. Over-represented, with A/G, among elite Thoroughbred racehorses in one study. No causal effect is established.

phenotypes.name: PDK4 A/G
phenotypes.description: One copy of each. Over-represented, with A/A, among elite Thoroughbred racehorses in one study. No causal effect is established.

phenotypes.name: PDK4 G/G
phenotypes.description: Two G copies. The genotype the Thoroughbred study found less often among elite racehorses; G was the commoner allele in Arabians. No causal effect is established.
